name: Capitals and punctuation ignored
a: Do you have a bachelor's degree?
b: DO YOU HAVE A BACHELOR'S DEGREE
spec_quote: Capitals, punctuation, curly vs straight apostrophes and other words do not matter.

name: Curly vs straight apostrophe
a: What's your major?
b: What’s your major?
spec_quote: Capitals, punctuation, curly vs straight apostrophes and other words do not matter.

name: AFTER graduation vs NOW
a: What degree will you hold?
b: What degree are you currently pursuing?
spec_quote: AFTER graduation (“once you've graduated”, “upon graduation”, “expected degree”, “will have / hold / earn”), NOW (“currently pursuing / enrolled”, “pursuing”, “in progress”)

name: AFTER expected degree vs COMPLETED highest
a: What is your expected degree?
b: What is your highest degree?
spec_quote: AFTER graduation (... “expected degree” ...), NOW (...), or COMPLETED (“highest”, “completed”, “attained”, “earned”, “obtained”) — each of these three is a separate mark

name: NOW enrolled vs COMPLETED obtained (same degree level, same yes/no form)
a: Are you currently enrolled in a master's program?
b: Have you obtained a master's degree?
spec_quote: each of these three is a separate mark; a wording may carry several;

name: Two AFTER wordings, both open
a: What degree will you earn?
b: What degree do you expect to hold upon graduation?
spec_quote: Two wordings stay together ("same") only when they agree on every one of these:

name: Two COMPLETED wordings, both open
a: What is your highest degree attained?
b: What degree have you obtained?
spec_quote: COMPLETED (“highest”, “completed”, “attained”, “earned”, “obtained”)

name: Two NOW wordings, both yes/no
a: Are you currently pursuing a degree?
b: Is your degree in progress?
spec_quote: NOW (“currently pursuing / enrolled”, “pursuing”, “in progress”)

name: Bachelor's named vs not named
a: Do you have a bachelor's degree?
b: Do you have a degree?
spec_quote: whether it names a bachelor's / undergraduate degree;

name: Bachelor's vs master's
a: What is your bachelor's degree?
b: What is your master's degree?
spec_quote: whether it names a bachelor's / undergraduate degree; whether it names a master's / graduate degree / PhD;

name: Master's vs PhD (single graduate-degree mark)
a: Do you have a master's degree?
b: Do you hold a PhD?
spec_quote: whether it names a master's / graduate degree / PhD;

name: Minor vs second major (single mark)
a: Do you have a minor?
b: Do you have a second major?
spec_quote: whether it is about a second / secondary / double major or a minor;

name: Minor named vs not named
a: Do you have a minor?
b: Do you have a degree?
spec_quote: whether it is about a second / secondary / double major or a minor;

name: Convicted vs criminal record (both crime)
a: Have you been convicted of a felony?
b: Do you have a criminal record?
spec_quote: whether it is about a crime (convicted, felony, criminal record, pleaded guilty);

name: Crime vs unrelated yes/no question
a: Have you ever been convicted of a crime?
b: Have you ever been fired from a job?
spec_quote: whether it is about a crime (convicted, felony, criminal record, pleaded guilty);

name: Any employer vs without restriction
a: Are you authorized to work for any employer?
b: Are you authorized to work without restriction?
spec_quote: whether it is about authorization for any / all employers or without restriction;

name: Plain work authorization vs all-employers authorization
a: Are you authorized to work in the United States?
b: Are you authorized to work for all employers?
spec_quote: whether it is about authorization for any / all employers or without restriction;

name: Same bachelor's content, yes/no vs open
a: Do you have a bachelor's degree?
b: Which bachelor's degree do you have?
spec_quote: whether it is a yes/no question (starts with are / is / do / does / did / will / would / can / could / have / has / had / were / was) or an open one (what / which / please …).

name: Same NOW content, yes/no vs open
a: Are you currently pursuing a degree?
b: What degree are you currently pursuing?
spec_quote: whether it is a yes/no question (starts with are / is / do / does / did / will / would / can / could / have / has / had / were / was) or an open one (what / which / please …).

name: Two open phrasings, please vs what
a: Please list your degrees.
b: What degrees do you hold?
spec_quote: an open one (what / which / please …).

name: Multi-mark: AFTER + bachelor's, both open
a: What bachelor's degree will you hold upon graduation?
b: What undergraduate degree will you earn once you've graduated?
spec_quote: a wording may carry several;

name: Multi-mark vs single-mark: AFTER present in only one
a: Will you have a bachelor's degree upon graduation?
b: Do you have a bachelor's degree?
spec_quote: each of these three is a separate mark; a wording may carry several;

name: Crime yes/no vs crime open (please)
a: Have you been convicted of a felony?
b: Please describe any criminal convictions.
spec_quote: whether it is a yes/no question (starts with are / is / do / does / did / will / would / can / could / have / has / had / were / was) or an open one (what / which / please …).

name: Extra words do not matter within crime yes/no
a: Do you have, or have you ever had, a criminal record?
b: Do you have a criminal record?
spec_quote: Capitals, punctuation, curly vs straight apostrophes and other words do not matter.

name: Two COMPLETED yes/no phrasings
a: Has your degree been completed?
b: Is your degree completed?
spec_quote: COMPLETED (“highest”, “completed”, “attained”, “earned”, “obtained”)
